commands.review_summary:
Adds a validated configurable session cookie name across API authentication, CSRF detection, desktop OAuth, generated protocol types, tests, and documentation while retaining `cc_session` as the default.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main uses the fixed `cc_session` name, so two services sharing a hostname cannot independently name their session cookies, and a foreign cookie can enter the cookie-CSRF path. The PR's regression test and live API transcript support that scenario, although no independent runtime reproduction was performed in this review.

target.title: feat(auth): support configurable session cookie names
target.body:
## Why

Running two ClickClack-compatible services on one hostname currently makes their browser sessions collide because both use `cc_session` and cookies ignore ports. A foreign instance cookie can also activate ClickClack's cookie-CSRF branch, rejecting an otherwise valid login.

## What changed

- Added `CLICKCLACK_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` with a validated, backward-compatible `cc_session` default.
- Routed session writes, auth reads, and CSRF cookie detection through the same configured name.
- Returned the effective name from desktop OAuth consume and updated desktop compatibility behavior.
- Updated the OpenAPI/generated SDK contract, docs, and shared-hostname isolation tests.

## Real behavior proof

On a live HTTPS ClickClack instance configured with `cc_stock_session`:

1. Sent magic-link consume with an existing foreign `cc_session` cookie.
2. Observed HTTP 200 instead of the prior CSRF 403.
3. Observed only `cc_stock_session` in `Set-Cookie`, with `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, and `SameSite=Lax` preserved.
4. Reused that cookie against `/api/me` and observed HTTP 200.

Redacted output from the live run:

```text
consume_status=200
set-cookie: cc_stock_session=<redacted>; Path=/; Expires=<redacted>; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax
me_status=200
```

The private host and bearer values are omitted. OAuth state/challenge cookie isolation and a packaged desktop end-to-end run were not tested; those cookies are unchanged by this PR.

## Compatibility

Servers that retain the default `cc_session` name remain compatible with existing desktop clients. A server configured with a custom name requires a desktop client containing this PR's additive `session_cookie_name` response handling; older desktop builds continue looking for `cc_session` and cannot complete desktop OAuth against that custom-name server.

## Validation

- `go test ./...`
- `pnpm check`
- `pnpm build`
- Independent attack-surface review: PASS
- Independent contract verification: PASS, 0 findings

## Risk

This changes authentication plumbing. The main invariant is that CSRF detection and auth lookup use the same single server field. Regression coverage proves a foreign default-name cookie is ignored when a custom name is configured. Empty configuration preserves `cc_session`; invalid names fail during config load.

## Review state

Local repository checks and independent security/contract review are complete. GitHub CI on Node 24 and GitHub Codex review remain merge conditions.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted. Authored by ragesaq, code by Chisel using OpenAI GPT-5.6-Sol, with independent Anthropic and Sentinel review. The resulting code and evidence were reviewed before publication.
